issues: Frame 4's completely empty eye band makes the midpoint read briefly as the eyes vanishing rather than clearly passing behind the barrel.
The tiny top and bottom stripe changes across frames 1-6 are so subtle at 1x that they can read as blue-pixel flicker rather than rotation.
The edge-eye slivers in frames 3 and 5 are slightly less immediately legible than the strong intermediate eye shapes in frames 2 and 6.
fixes: In frame 3, clarify the departing left-edge eye with one additional contiguous white pixel; mirror that treatment on the right-edge eye in frame 5.
In frame 4, consider retaining a single white edge pixel on one side of the band to preserve rotational direction through the rear-facing pose.
Make one blue stripe cluster in frames 2-5 shift as a coherent 2-3-pixel unit rather than relying mainly on isolated single-pixel swaps, while keeping the silhouette fixed.

issues: Frames 3 and 4 have very sparse eye-band changes, so the rotation reads slightly slower through the rear-facing portion than through frames 5, 6, and 1.
The partially occluded eye at the right side of frame 5 reads somewhat like a background-colored notch before becoming clearly identifiable in frame 6.
fixes: In frame 4, advance one edge pixel of the rear band or an aligned top/bottom stripe by one pixel to strengthen the rotational phase without changing the silhouette.
In frame 5, expose a single white leading pixel of the entering eye at the right edge, while retaining its black pupil/occlusion cluster, to make the transition into frame 6 clearer.

issues: Frame 4 loses the eye band almost completely, making the middle read as an empty white barrel rather than the back phase of a rotating band.
The edge-on eye fragments in frames 3 and 5 form cramped, hook-like clusters; they read more as broken pieces than clean cylindrical foreshortening.
Frames 2 and 6 do not make a fully convincing mirrored pair around the front-facing frame 1, so the wraparound path of the eyes feels slightly uneven.
The top and bottom stripe changes are very small and can read as isolated pixel flicker rather than clearly supporting the same rotation.
The silhouette remains stable and every loop step contains deliberate changes, but the six-frame sequence is more elaborate than its limited visual payoff warrants.
fixes: In frame 4, retain a one-pixel dark-blue or black horizontal seam across part of the middle so the rotating eye band remains structurally legible on the back side.
Redraw the visible band edges in frames 3 and 5 as clean one- or two-pixel vertical slivers attached to the barrel edge; remove the hook-shaped interior cavities.
Make frames 2 and 6 exact perspective counterparts: match the widths, pupil clipping, and spacing of the eyes while reversing their horizontal placement.
In frames 2-5, move the top and bottom blue stripe clusters through a consistent one-pixel horizontal progression instead of changing isolated points.
Preserve the locked outer silhouette, but simplify the middle phases to four stronger rotational poses if cartridge-style animation economy is the priority.

issues: Frames 3-5 lose the eye-band cue: frame 3 reduces it to a small edge fragment, frame 4 has an entirely blank black band, and frame 5 introduces a low-contrast C-shaped mark. The rotation therefore reads more as eyes vanishing and reappearing than as a continuous wraparound spin.
The dark C-shaped cluster in frame 5 reads like a dent or stray interior mark rather than a foreshortened eye.
The eye transition from frame 6 back to frame 1 is comparatively abrupt, snapping from one clear eye plus a dark fragment to two fully presented eyes.

Several lower-barrel stripe clusters in frames 2-3 are more stepped and irregular than the clean vertical stripe language on the upper barrel, weakening the sense that both sections share one rotation.
fixes: In frame 3, reshape the retreating eye into a clean one-pixel-wide light crescent at the left edge of the band instead of the ambiguous compact fragment.
In frame 4, retain a single one-pixel dark-blue or gray edge sliver at the opposite side of the band so the rear-facing phase still communicates continued rotation.
In frame 5, replace the dark C-shaped cluster with a narrow light crescent entering from the right, then widen that same cluster in frame 6 before reaching the full eye in frame 1.

Regularize the lower stripes in frames 2-3 into the same one- and two-pixel vertical columns used on the upper barrel, shifting them horizontally one pixel per phase rather than changing their cluster shape.

issues: Frame 5's narrow side-on eye cluster is slightly abstract at 1x and can momentarily read as a loose dark notch.
Frames 3 and 4 are both eyeless, so the middle of the rotation depends mainly on the moving blue stripes.
The frame 6-to-frame 1 transition has a somewhat stronger visual pop as the second eye rotates fully into view.
fixes: In frame 5, add a one-pixel white glint inside the side-eye cluster while preserving its wrapped profile.
In frame 4, shift one central stripe edge by one pixel to distinguish its rotational phase more strongly from frame 3.
In frame 6, expose one additional white pixel at the incoming left eye edge to soften the transition into frame 1.
